definition: An organic compound whose molecules carry the carboxyl group -COOH on an end carbon. A homologous series of weak acids formed by oxidising alcohols.
msAccepts: weak organic acid from alcohol oxidation
homologous series with the carboxyl group

definition: The atom or bond arrangement that gives an organic family its characteristic reactions. For the carboxylic acids it is -COOH; for the alcohols it was -OH.
msAccepts: the reactive arrangement determining chemical properties
msAvoids: giving -OH as the acid family's group

definition: The -COOH arrangement: a carbonyl C=O and a hydroxyl O-H sharing the same end carbon atom. Always terminal, which is why no locant appears in acid names.
msAccepts: C=O and O-H on the same carbon
always at the end of the chain
msAvoids: drawing only one of the two bonds

definition: The carboxylic acid CH3COOH (C2H4O2): vinegar's acid, the family's representative, and the oxidation product of ethanol.
msAccepts: the acid in vinegar properly called ethanoic acid
msAvoids: calling it 'acetic' only when the systematic name is asked

definition: An aqueous solution containing ethanoic acid — the everyday representative of the carboxylic acid family, sour to taste and below pH 7.
msAccepts: a dilute solution of ethanoic acid
msAvoids: saying vinegar is ethanol or a different acid

definition: The one-carbon carboxylic acid HCOOH (CH2O2): the family's smallest member, carried in nettle stings.
msAvoids: counting zero carbons (the carboxyl carbon is the one carbon)

definition: The three-carbon carboxylic acid CH3CH2COOH (C3H6O2): 'prop' counts the two chain carbons plus the carboxyl carbon.
msAvoids: counting only the CH3CH2- part (two carbons)
adding a locant number to the name

definition: The four-carbon carboxylic acid CH3CH2CH2COOH (C4H8O2): the largest member the specification requires.
A formula counting the atoms of each element in one molecule — C2H4O2 for ethanoic acid — without showing how they are joined.
msAccepts: shows what but not how joined
msAvoids: omitting the second oxygen of the acid family

definition: A condensed formula showing the order of atoms unambiguously — CH3CH2COOH — without drawing every bond.
msAccepts: shows atom order in condensed form
msAvoids: drawing all bonds when condensed form is asked

definition: A drawing showing every atom and every bond as an explicit line. For carboxylic acids the COOH end must show both the C=O and the O-H.
msAccepts: the C=O and O-H of COOH both explicit
msAvoids: writing the condensed COOH when a display is asked

definition: A family of compounds with the same functional group, similar chemical properties, and consecutive members differing by a -CH2- unit — here the carboxylic acids.
An acid that dissociates only partially in water — ethanoic acid ionises about 1 molecule in 75 — giving fewer H+ ions and slower reactions than strong acids at equal concentration.
msAccepts: lower H+ concentration than a strong acid at the same concentration
msAvoids: saying weak acids do not react

definition: An acid that dissociates completely into ions in water — hydrochloric or sulfuric acid — so its solution holds mostly ions and hardly any intact molecules.
msAccepts: mostly H+ and anions in solution

definition: The splitting of an acid molecule into ions when it dissolves in water. Complete for strong acids, partial for weak ones — the measure behind the strength label.
msAccepts: complete for strong acids, partial for weak
produces H+ ions and the anion

definition: A solution holding a large amount of acid per unit volume — a concentration statement, independent of whether the acid is strong or weak.
msAccepts: large amount of acid per volume

definition: The ionic compound formed when an acid's H+ is replaced by a metal ion — here a metal ethanoate, built from the metal cation and the ethanoate anion.
msAccepts: ionic compound from acid plus metal or carbonate
formed with hydrogen gas from metals or CO2 from carbonates
msAvoids: calling CO2 part of the salt
writing the salt formula without charge balancing

definition: The singly-charged negative ion CH3COO-, the carboxylic-acid molecule with its acidic hydrogen removed; the anion of every ethanoate salt.
msAvoids: giving it a 2- charge (two ions balance Mg2+)

definition: A compound of oppositely charged ions held by electrostatic attraction — magnesium ethanoate holds Mg2+ attracted to the negative oxygens of two ethanoate ions.
msAccepts: positive and negative ions attracted together
msAvoids: treating the salt as covalent molecules

definition: The ranking of metals by reactivity. Metals above hydrogen react with acids giving salt plus hydrogen; metals below hydrogen — copper, silver — do not react.
msAccepts: metals above hydrogen react with acids
orders sodium above zinc above hydrogen above copper
msAvoids: saying all metals react with acids

definition: An ionic compound bearing the doubly-charged carbonate ion CO32-. Reacts with acids to give a salt, carbon dioxide and water.
msAccepts: acid + carbonate gives salt + CO2 + water
needs two protons per carbonate ion
msAvoids: balancing with one acid molecule per carbonate
